body.statement: For \(r=C_{\mathrm{scale}}\rho_\star\), can \(H_{\mathrm{occ}}\) construct one finite family \(\{Q_t:t\in\mathcal G_r\}\) on the full class \(\mathcal M_H\) such that \(\sup_{D_n\sim_1D_n'}|Q_t(D_n)-Q_t(D_n')|\le1\) for every \(t\), \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C_{\mathrm{shell}}\), and \(C_{\mathrm{shell}}\) is independent of the Hölder-sieve dimension, uniformly over all values of \(n\ell^d\)?
body.justification: This is the genuine construction problem: the occupancy identity must survive profiling over every unknown propensity and outcome-regression nuisance without an entropy payment.
body.gap: The downgraded parent reaches only a sparse shared-sign family, while Asi et al. and Chaudhuri et al. do not provide nuisance-independent composite CATE fiber scores.
body.consumer: An affirmative answer combines with the shell proposition and the same-class lower bound to settle the pure-private pointwise-CATE frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct explicit target-indexed scores \(Q_t\) on the entire composite class \(\mathcal M_H\) and prove the uniform weighted-shell bound \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C_{\mathrm{shell}}\) at \(r=C_{\mathrm{scale}}\rho_\star\).
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle specifies procedural verbs but no score formula, nuisance sieve, clipping envelope, or composite-test separation inequality. The occupancy lemma controls the mean and sensitivity of one fixed pair kernel; it does not show that profiled full-fiber kernels retain a common signed separation, and the shell proposition assumes rather than proves the required weighted tail sum.
obligation.attempted: Occupancy-weighted fixed-kernel scores close on a shared-sign two-fiber subfamily, but profiling finite nuisance sieves introduces an uncovered entropy factor. Replacing the scores by direct local treated/control averages gives a valid full-class private estimator, but only at the slower regression rate recorded below and therefore does not certify the requested rho-star shell family.
obligation.partial_result:
An unconditional loose upper bound is nevertheless obtainable on the same
class.  For a cube \(B_H\) of side \(H\) about \(x_0\), form
\(N_a=\sum_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_H,A_i=a\}\) and
\(S_a=\sum_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_H,A_i=a\}Y_i\).  Release the four-vector
\((N_0,N_1,S_0,S_1)\) with independent Laplace noise of scale
\(8/\epsilon\), and set
\[
 \widehat\mu_a=
 \Pi_{[-1,1]}\!\left(
 \frac{\widetilde S_a}{\max\{\widetilde N_a,e_0nH^d/2\}}
 \right),\qquad
 \widehat\theta_H=\Pi_{[-2,2]}(\widehat\mu_1-\widehat\mu_0).
\]
The vector has replacement \(\ell_1\)-sensitivity at most four, so this
release is pure \(\epsilon\)-private.  Uniform design and overlap give
\(\mathbb EN_a\ge e_0nH^d\).  Since
\(\mu_1=\mu_0+\tau\) and \(q<\gamma\) imply that both regressions are
\(\beta\)-Hölder, bounded-variable concentration and the first absolute
moment of Laplace noise give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_H-\theta(P)|
 \le C\left\{H^\beta+(nH^d)^{-1/2}+(n\epsilon H^d)^{-1}\right\}.
\]
Taking
\(H\asymp n^{-1/(2\beta+d)}\vee(n\epsilon)^{-1/(\beta+d)}\), truncated at
\(1/4\), proves the honest bracket
\[
 c\rho_\star\le R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \le C\left[1\wedge\left\{
 n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee
 (n\epsilon)^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\right\}\right].
\]
This does not prove the requested \(\rho_\star\)-scale score family: it is a
first-order regression fallback and can be strictly slower than the desired
two-fiber rate.
